method.principle: Only encode a causal or mechanistic edge when the relation has explicit provenance, an evidence design, a bounded scope, and a rationale. Patent disclosure, citation, family membership, timing, and co-occurrence are not treated as causal evidence.
causal_hierarchy: Randomized comparisons may support a total treatment effect for the enrolled population, comparator, endpoint, and follow-up window.
Controlled preclinical experiments may support mechanistic causality only in the tested model.
Regulatory statements may support an established mechanism or recognized safety mechanism, while preserving the label's scope.
Non-randomized subgroup differences are encoded as associative unless confounding is adequately controlled.

concepts.label: Durvalumab
concepts.description: Human monoclonal antibody directed against PD-L1.

concepts.label: PD-L1 interaction with PD-1 and CD80
concepts.description: Checkpoint interactions through which PD-L1 suppresses antitumor T-cell activity.

concepts.label: T-cell inhibition
concepts.description: Inhibitory checkpoint signaling that limits T-cell activation and antitumor immune responses.

concepts.label: T-cell activation
concepts.description: Restored or increased T-cell activity after PD-L1 blockade in preclinical experiments.

concepts.label: Tumor growth in human-immune-cell xenograft models
concepts.description: Preclinical tumor-growth outcome; it is not a human clinical endpoint.

concepts.label: Durvalumab after concurrent chemoradiotherapy
concepts.description: Consolidation durvalumab in unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after platinum-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy.

concepts.label: Disease progression or death
concepts.description: Progression-free survival endpoint used in the PACIFIC randomized trial.

concepts.label: Overall survival
concepts.description: Time-to-death endpoint reported in PACIFIC follow-up.

concepts.label: Immune-mediated adverse reactions
concepts.description: Adverse reactions caused by loss of immune inhibition and peripheral tolerance after PD-1/PD-L1 pathway blockade.

concepts.label: Pneumonitis or radiation pneumonitis
concepts.description: Composite pulmonary safety outcome reported for PACIFIC; mixed immune and radiation etiologies limit mechanism-specific interpretation.

concepts.label: Recent thoracic radiation
concepts.description: Recent thoracic radiation exposure before PD-L1 therapy; not randomized as an exposure in the cited safety comparison.

evidence.conclusion_or_fact: Preclinical characterization found that MEDI4736 bound PD-L1, blocked PD-L1 interactions with PD-1 and CD80, restored T-cell activation, and produced T-cell-dependent antitumor activity in xenograft models.
evidence.scope: In vitro assays and human-immune-cell xenograft models; no direct inference of human clinical benefit.

evidence.conclusion_or_fact: The FDA label describes PD-L1-mediated T-cell inhibition and states that durvalumab blocks PD-L1 binding to PD-1 and CD80, releasing inhibition of PD-L1-mediated immune responses.
evidence.scope: Regulatory mechanism-of-action statement, supported by nonclinical evidence.

evidence.conclusion_or_fact: In PACIFIC, randomization to durvalumab after concurrent chemoradiotherapy improved progression-free survival versus placebo; the reported hazard ratio was 0.52 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.42 to 0.65.
evidence.scope: Unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after at least two cycles of platinum-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy.

evidence.conclusion_or_fact: Five-year PACIFIC follow-up reported an overall-survival hazard ratio of 0.72, with estimated five-year survival of 42.9% for durvalumab and 33.4% for placebo.
evidence.scope: Long-term follow-up of the randomized PACIFIC population.

evidence.conclusion_or_fact: The FDA label states that PD-1/PD-L1 pathway blockade can break peripheral tolerance and induce immune-mediated adverse reactions.
evidence.scope: Class-mechanism safety statement; event-specific risk varies by organ, regimen, and population.

evidence.conclusion_or_fact: In PACIFIC, pneumonitis including radiation pneumonitis occurred in 18.3% of durvalumab-treated patients and 12.8% of placebo-treated patients after recent radiation.
evidence.scope: PACIFIC safety population after definitive chemoradiation; outcome combines pneumonitis and radiation pneumonitis.

relations.rationale: Direct binding and blockade were characterized experimentally and are described in the current regulatory mechanism-of-action section.

properties.scope: Molecular target engagement; not itself a clinical efficacy claim.

relations.rationale: The regulatory mechanism states that PD-L1 interaction with PD-1 and CD80 inhibits T-cell activation and cytokine production.
Durvalumab blocks the PD-L1 interactions that transmit inhibitory checkpoint signaling.

properties.mediator: PD-L1 interaction with PD-1 and CD80

relations.rationale: Restored T-cell activation was observed after PD-L1 blockade in preclinical assays; the inference is bounded to those experimental systems.

properties.scope: In vitro and nonclinical immune-response models; no direct clinical endpoint.

relations.rationale: The reported antitumor effect was T-cell dependent, supporting a mediated causal path in the xenograft model but not establishing human benefit.

properties.extrapolation_limit: Do not promote this edge to a human clinical outcome.

relations.rationale: The randomized, placebo-controlled PACIFIC comparison identifies a total treatment effect for progression-free survival in the enrolled population.

properties.population: Unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after platinum-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy

relations.rationale: Long-term follow-up of the randomized PACIFIC comparison supports a total survival effect for the trial population.
The label attributes immune-mediated adverse reactions to removal of PD-1/PD-L1 pathway inhibition and loss of peripheral tolerance.

properties.scope: Class-mechanism safety relationship; not an organ-specific incidence estimate.

relations.rationale: Randomization supports a treatment-attributable difference in the composite pneumonitis outcome, but mixed immune and radiation etiologies limit mechanism-specific certainty.

properties.population: PACIFIC safety population after definitive chemoradiation

relations.rationale: The label reports a higher incidence after recent thoracic radiation, but radiation exposure was not randomized in this comparison and the outcome has mixed etiologies; the edge therefore does not assert causation.

properties.causal_limit: Potential confounding and mixed pneumonitis attribution.
